The previous owner never waterproofed the basement. And living in a place where we see all 4 seasons, plus the occasional hurricane, it's a good idea to waterproof it. But, once the house is built, most people will only waterproof the inside. While that's good, it doesn't prevent water from getting inside the wall. Moisture inside the blocks can deteriorate the cement holding them together, which can break down much faster. Once the basement walls go, it's over. It's always better to spend the extra few thousand to ge the ground dug up and waterproof the outside.

My dad is a retired mason so he spent the better part of his life doing blockwork. He also remodeled the house I grew up in. So, I know the kind of work he does.
